absent: Full buffer_head, folio, address_space, inode and writeback_control layouts beyond the fields and helpers mentioned in the fragments.
Semantics of folio helpers, block size helpers, buffer state tests, dirty marking, zeroing, submission and wait primitives beyond their call sites.
Filesystem get_block implementations, block to sector mapping details and on-disk format.
Common full folio write path, end I/O handlers and I/O flag meanings beyond the shown invocations.
Slab cache options, per-CPU mechanics, cpuhotplug states, LRU sizing and buffer accounting thresholds.
Character number limits, dynamic range markers, minor mask width and device identifier encoding.
kobj_map, kobject, device, module reference and file_operations lifetimes beyond the shown calls.
ELF 32-bit type layouts, loader flow and compat helper implementations behind the alias names.
Coredump pattern language, CORENAME_MAX_SIZE value, trace point list and pipe handling.
Error code numeric values and logging output formats.

findings.text: Provides a helper that prepares the tail of a file whose new end falls inside a filesystem block. If the offset sits on a block edge there is nothing to do. Otherwise it locates the folio holding the offset, ensures buffer descriptors exist, walks to the descriptor covering the offset while advancing the logical block number, instantiates a mapping through get_block supplied by the caller when needed, treats an unmapped result as a hole with no further work, brings the mapped portion current by marking or reading as required by present state flags, then clears the trailing region and marks the descriptor dirty before releasing the folio. Errors from folio acquisition, mapping or reading are propagated.

Offers a small inline read helper for a single buffer descriptor. It first probes whether the descriptor is already current or can be claimed without blocking work, reporting immediate success when that probe succeeds. Otherwise it delegates to the locked read path with waiting enabled and caller operation flags passed through, returning that path outcome.

Implements writeback for a whole folio in the block mapping path. A folio entirely below the current file size goes directly to the common write path. A folio starting at or beyond the size is treated as racing with truncation, unlocked, and reported as success without I/O. A folio straddling the size has its beyond-end portion cleared on every invocation to preserve mapped zero semantics before delegating to the common write path.

Provides block number translation using the filesystem block resolver. It sizes a transient on-stack descriptor from the host inode block size, invokes the resolver for the requested logical block without creation, and returns the resulting device block number.

Defines synchronous flushing for a dirty buffer descriptor plus a convenience wrapper that supplies synchronous operation flags. The core routine asserts a live reference, claims the buffer lock, and if a dirty marker was present requires a mapped state before submitting a write and waiting for completion, with loss of currency after the wait reported as I/O failure. If no dirty marker was present it simply releases the lock and reports success, as does a successful write.

The cache holder named bh_cachep and the ceiling named max_buffer_heads become immutable after early boot. The flag named buffer_heads_over_limit signals excess occupancy. Accounting uses a record named bh_accounting with a live total named nr plus a dampening value named ratelimit, kept as a per-processor instance also named bh_accounting starting from zero.

Defines offline-processor cleanup for buffer caching. It releases every slot in the departing processor local least-recently-used table and clears those slots, then folds the departing processor live total into the current processor total and resets the departed total to zero before reporting success.

Specifies a check then claim discipline for buffer currency. If the descriptor already appears current it reports success without locking. Otherwise it acquires the buffer lock, rechecks currency, keeps the lock held on behalf of the caller when still not current, and otherwise releases the lock and reports success.

Requires the caller to hold the buffer lock, then submits a read operation with caller flags and a read completion routine. When waiting is requested it sleeps until completion and converts lack of currency into an I/O error, while without waiting it returns immediately with success.

Submits reads for a caller supplied array. Entries already current are skipped. Remaining entries are locked either unconditionally or opportunistically depending on a force indicator, with opportunistic failures skipped. After locking, entries that became current are unlocked and skipped, while the rest are submitted for reading without waiting.

Early initialization for the buffer layer. It creates a reclaim-accounted panicking slab for descriptors, derives a live-descriptor ceiling as ten percent of free buffer pages scaled by how many descriptors fit per page, and registers a no-call teardown handler for processor removal, warning if registration fails.

Lays out the character number registry. A pointer named cdev_map holds the number to object mapping and becomes immutable after early boot. Protection uses a mutex named chrdevs_lock. Hashing uses a fixed bucket total. Each registry record stores a major identity plus a name area plus linkage via next plus an associated cdev pointer documented as legacy plus a baseminor start plus a minorct span. Buckets live in an array named chrdevs indexed by hashed major.
Maps a major number to a hash bucket by remainder against the bucket total.

Exposes registered character names for proc-style display. Under registry mutex protection it walks the bucket selected by the supplied offset and emits major plus name lines for entries whose major equals that offset.

Allocates dynamic majors by descending search. It first seeks a completely empty top bucket from the array end down to the dynamic end marker. If none is empty it scans an extended interval from start down to end, treating a major as free when no entry in its bucket carries that major. Failure in both scans yields a busy error.

Governs insertion of a character number interval. It rejects majors beyond the allowed maximum and minor spans extending past the per-major mask with invalid errors, rejects allocation failure with out-of-memory, and under mutex protection assigns a dynamic major when zero was requested, failing with busy when exhausted. It then locates the sorted position inside the hashed bucket, skipping lower majors and non-overlapping lower ranges, stopping at higher majors or higher non-overlapping ranges, and rejects any overlap with busy. On success it fills major and baseminor start and minorct span and name and splices the record into the chain.

Removes an exact number interval. Under mutex protection it searches the hashed bucket by pointer to pointer linkage for an entry matching major plus base minor plus span together, unlinks it when found, releases the mutex, and returns the removed record or null when absent.

Provides range registration spanning majors with atomicity. The register path splits the caller interval at each major boundary, registers each piece, and on any piece failure unwinds all earlier pieces before propagating the error. The unregister path splits identically and releases each piece.

Allocates a dynamic character interval. It delegates to the internal region allocator with a zero major request and on success composes the output device identifier from the allocated major and base minor.

Combines number allocation with legacy device object creation. It first reserves the number interval, allocates a dynamic device object, assigns the owner field from operations owner and the ops field from operations, names the embedded kobj, and adds it at the composed device number. On add failure it drops the object reference, on allocation failure it unwinds the number reservation. Success with an explicit major reports zero, while success with a dynamic request reports the allocated major.
Legacy unregistration removes the number interval then deletes the linked device object when present before freeing the registry record.

Lifecycle for mapping a device object to numbers. Add records the device number and span in the object, rejects the whiteout identifier with busy, maps the range through the global map with exact matching helpers, and on success pins the parent object, while on failure it clears the freed name. Delete removes the mapping then drops the object reference. Unmap is a thin removal of the mapping for a device span.
Allocates a zeroed dynamic device object, initializes its device list linkage, and initializes its embedded object with the dynamic release type before returning it.

Protects device object lookup and inode linkage with a cache aligned spinlock. Acquisition takes a module reference then a kobject reference unless already zero, releasing the module reference if the latter fails. Release drops the kobject reference then the module reference, tolerating a null pointer.

Opens a character inode by binding it to its device object. Under spinlock protection it reuses a cached binding when present, otherwise drops the lock to look up the global map, then reacquires and revalidates to handle races, installing the winner and linking the inode when still unbound. Reference acquisition failure yields no-device errors. After binding it obtains the operations pointer, replaces the file operations, invokes the driver open when present, and on any failure after binding drops the device reference before returning no-device or the driver status.
Defines file operation replacement as releasing the prior operations reference and then installing the supplied pointer, asserting the new pointer is non-null.

Detaches every inode bound to a device object. Under spinlock protection it repeatedly removes the first list element, reinitializes its linkage, and clears its cached device pointer until the list is empty.

Supplies default character file behavior with open bound to the character open routine and seek bound to a no-op seek. Exact matching returns the embedded object from opaque data regardless of device and partition inputs, while exact locking acquires the device reference and reports zero on success or negative one on failure.

Manages parent linkage and combined device registration. Setting a parent warns unless the parent object was initialized, then records it. Combined add maps the device number when the device carries one before adding the device, unwinding the mapping if the device add fails. Combined delete removes the device first and then the mapping when a device number is present.

Distinguishes static and dynamic teardown. Both purge bound inodes and release the parent reference, with the dynamic variant additionally freeing the containing structure. Two type records bind the default and dynamic release routines respectively.

Covers initialization helpers. Init clears a device object, sets up its list and default type, and records supplied operations. Base probing attempts to load a major-minor aliased module and on positive success also tries a major-only alias before returning null. Character subsystem init creates the global number map with the base probe and the registry mutex.
The character registry hash uses 255 buckets.
Compatibility ELF mode is enabled with value 1, the ELF class selects ELFCLASS32, and additional page setup presence is enabled with value 1.
Generic header names resolve to 32-bit forms. Name elfhdr maps to elf32_hdr, with elf_phdr mapping to elf32_phdr, plus elf_shdr mapping to elf32_shdr.
Further generic names resolve to 32-bit forms. elf_note maps to elf32_note, with elf_addr_t mapping to Elf32_Addr, plus property alignment mapping to ELF32_GNU_PROPERTY_ALIGN.

Basic compat types redirect. user_long_t becomes compat_long_t, with user_siginfo_t becoming compat_siginfo_t, plus copy_siginfo_to_external becoming copy_siginfo_to_external32. Time helper ns_to_kernel_old_timeval becomes ns_to_old_timeval32, and elf_check_arch becomes compat_elf_check_arch.
Compat process status names redirect. elf_prstatus becomes compat_elf_prstatus, with elf_prstatus_common becoming compat_elf_prstatus_common, plus elf_prpsinfo becoming compat_elf_prpsinfo.
Platform capability names redirect. ELF_PLATFORM becomes COMPAT_ELF_PLATFORM, with ELF_HWCAP becoming COMPAT_ELF_HWCAP, plus ELF_HWCAP2 becoming COMPAT_ELF_HWCAP2.
Further capability and boot info redirect. ELF_HWCAP3 becomes COMPAT_ELF_HWCAP3, with ELF_HWCAP4 becoming COMPAT_ELF_HWCAP4, plus ARCH_DLINFO becoming COMPAT_ARCH_DLINFO.
Load and personality names redirect. ELF_ET_DYN_BASE becomes COMPAT_ELF_ET_DYN_BASE, with ELF_PLAT_INIT becoming COMPAT_ELF_PLAT_INIT, plus SET_PERSONALITY becoming COMPAT_SET_PERSONALITY.

Thread start redirects to compat. COMPAT_START_THREAD accepts ex plus regs plus new_ip plus new_sp and forwards only regs plus new_ip plus new_sp to compat_start_thread, while START_THREAD resolves to COMPAT_START_THREAD.

Additional page setup and exec implication redirect. COMPAT_ARCH_SETUP_ADDITIONAL_PAGES accepts bprm plus ex plus interpreter and forwards only bprm plus interpreter to compat_arch_setup_additional_pages. The presence flag ARCH_HAS_SETUP_ADDITIONAL_PAGES is enabled, generic ARCH_SETUP_ADDITIONAL_PAGES resolves to the compat variant, and elf_read_implies_exec resolves to compat_elf_read_implies_exec.

ELF format and test names redirect to compat. elf_format becomes compat_elf_format, with init_elf_binfmt becoming init_compat_elf_binfmt, plus exit_elf_binfmt becoming exit_compat_elf_binfmt, plus binfmt_elf_test_cases becoming compat_binfmt_elf_test_cases, plus binfmt_elf_test_suite becoming compat_binfmt_elf_test_suite.
Enables trace point creation for the coredump component.
Default file note size limit is 4194304 bytes, maximum is 16777216 bytes, and the coredump pidfd number is 3.

Coredump control state combines scalars, a pattern buffer and a builder record with a type tag. Scalars include core_uses_pid flag plus core_pipe_limit ceiling plus core_sort_vma selector plus core_name_size capacity plus core_file_note_size_limit initialized from the default plus core_pipe_count atomic starting at zero. Pattern storage core_pattern defaults to core text. Type tag coredump_type_t distinguishes COREDUMP_FILE as one and COREDUMP_PIPE as two and COREDUMP_SOCK as three and COREDUMP_SOCK_REQ as four. Builder core_name holds a corename pointer sized by size, together with used progress and size capacity and a pipe ceiling and a dumped marker and a core_type tag and a mask filter.

Pattern builder grows and appends safely. Expansion rounds the requested size, reallocates the corename buffer, updates size, and raises a shared high-water mark when larger. Formatted append measures needed space with a copied argument list, advances used on fit, otherwise grows by the shortfall plus one and retries, reporting out-of-memory when growth fails. A variadic wrapper forwards to the va_list form.

Registry mutex discipline. The chrdevs_lock mutex is held while walking buckets for display, while searching and splicing during region insertion including dynamic allocation, and while searching and unlinking during exact removal.

Buffer and folio locking order. Truncation holds the folio lock across descriptor setup, mapping, reading, zeroing and dirtying before unlock and release. Synchronous flushing claims the buffer lock and holds it across dirty clearing, submission and waiting. Uptodate checks either observe currency lock-free or claim the lock for the slow path. Batch submission never sleeps for locks unless forced.

Buffer hazards include size mismatch warnings, holes treated as success without I/O, read failures propagated without zeroing, unmapped synchronous flush failing as I/O error for hot-removal, and post-wait loss of currency reported as I/O error. Batch path silently skips contended entries.

Character registry hazards cover invalid major and minor span rejections, out-of-memory during record allocation, busy on dynamic exhaustion and on overlapping intervals, whiteout device rejection, missing map lookup and failed reference acquisition during open reported as no-device, missing operations and driver open failures unwound with reference drops, and partial multi-major registration rolled back.

Coredump builder hazards are allocation failures during growth and formatted append, both reported as out-of-memory without altering completed length beyond prior content, plus a racy but harmless high-water update.
